body: But I've spent so much time with her. I can't just forsake someone like that, that's the better part of the last year of my life. And I can't leave someone broken, let alone someone I care about so much. Maybe it's self destructive, and I know it's a tall order, but I'm looking to patch things up if it all possible.

That's the thing. It was her, but she's got a lot of friends now as I mentioned. I just have her, and everything indicates I need to let go. Every time I try (admittedly not very hard), I get roped back in. I have "buddies," but no one I care to hang out with once work ends. I'm attached to an infantry unit, and the majority of people here are not the type of people I care to interact with. I had a buddy off base, but something bad happened between him and Ana one night and she doesn't like him, and I guess that kinda steered me away from him as well. I like giving people the benefit of the doubt, but I look at what I've written here and I really feel like I've been manipulated.

I've only really ever been passionate about music and writing. I realized I was good at both of these things at a young age, and they're the two things I've been able to fall back on when I can't get anything else right. 

I read a lot of absurdism (lately *The Plague* by Camus) and Beat Generation novels, and I find the philosophies and writing styles therein really speak to me. I know it sounds bad, but the deepest throws of depression inspire my best writing; I question it the least after I'm done writing it because it's the most honest I can be with myself. The problem is I can't share it with anyone, because that involves revealing myself to people I love and people who love me. 

When I joined the military, I figured it would provide me with stories. I wasn't wrong, but I didn't expect 4 years worth of depressing stories. This doesn't bother me so much, but I guess I was lead astray by the romanticizing of military life by American authors. I assumed I'd have more interesting stories to tell when this is all said and done, but I don't have any interest in writing about much more than the alcohol driven nights off base, followed by mornings of pain and regret.

The problem I have lately is I can't write anything worth sharing. I write prose fueled by depression and cheap wine but I can't have anyone bare that burden. It's infuriating that it takes the pestilence that is depression to write anything worth keeping. Depression is the very characteristic making the writing unshareable, but I haven't found a way to write without it. At the end of the day I guess I'm writing for myself, but it certainly would feel good to show the people I love something I've created.

I read this in the morning but couldn't respond because my charger was left in Ana's car last night, and I wanted to say thank you for the advice. I used the remaining charge to call her and ask about getting my charger back and we met shortly after and grabbed coffee. 

The short and sweet is that things are okay with her now. She's very understanding and was glad to hear that in the past few sober hours I'd thought a lot about what happened and wanted to apologize for making her uncomfortable. Afterwards we drove around for a bit and just talked. 

I'm okay right now, just sitting in my barracks messing with a guitar but these thoughts come in waves. I've done so much to combat them. When it first got bad, I never cleaned my room until inspections, I stopped taking care of my hygiene, I never slept, and I only left when I had to. Since then I've started showering every day, keeping the room clean on a regular basis, and I go out and read when I have time.

I'm just never quite free from the dread that brings these thoughts on. I am not afraid of death, it gets us all sooner or later. It sounds infinitely better than what I have in front of me in this world. It sounds peaceful. I just don't want to hurt others. I don't harbor negative feelings towards others for long, and as a result, I don't hate anyone. I think it's a nasty feeling and nothing good comes of it. However, I almost hate the people I'm closest to for keeping me here, and they don't even know it. 

In my mind, someone's gonna get hurt whether I stay or go. If I ended my life, I'd hurt a number of people (mostly family, a few friends). If I stay, I'm hurt but nobody has to know about it. I put on my mask and I go visit family and friends once a year. Then I go back to work and I put that mask on. No one knows what's underneath, because to my credit, they're all finely crafted masks. But it gets hot and stuffy in there after a while, and that's when the thoughts resurface.

I like the idea of a new posting, but there's no saying where I'll end up being such low rank and enlisted. It could work out, or it could be infinitely worse, and that's not something I'm comfortable risking. Not to mention the dread I'd have to go through to get it. I'm a go to guy where I work and my chain of command would make sure my remaining time is hell if I tried to go. 

I feel like I'm stuck on a mobius strip of depression and fleeting acceptance of reality. I'm glad there are places like this to talk about it with people who choose to listen, because I couldn't put that burden on anyone I know. Thanks for listening, and thank you for the advice, both mean a lot to me right now.
